pages.text: Mila opens a big world map at school. She wonders how children in many places say hello.
Her friend Ana waves and says, Hola! Mila learns that Hola means hello in Spanish.
Next, their teacher smiles and says, Bonjour! Mila learns that Bonjour is hello in French.
On a class video call, a child in Japan says Konnichiwa. Mila hears another friendly hello.
Mila notices people also greet with a wave, a bow, or a handshake depending on place and custom.
No matter the word, a warm face and gentle voice can make others feel safe and included.
At recess, children try hello words from home. The playground sounds bright and joyful.
Mila practices: Hola, Bonjour, and Konnichiwa. She speaks slowly and listens carefully.
She learns a big idea: greetings can sound different, but kindness feels the same.
Before bed, Mila remembers three hello words and one rule: greet people with respect.
